question: What does semantic HTML mean, and why do interviewers care?
shortAnswer: Using elements for meaning (header, nav, main, article) rather than only divs for layout.
detailedAnswer: Semantic tags communicate document structure to browsers, assistive tech, and crawlers. They improve accessibility tree quality, default keyboard behavior, and SEO signals. Layout still uses CSS; semantics describe role. Prefer button over clickable divs, and lists for list content.
interviewTip: Tie semantics to a11y + SEO, not just clean code.
commonMistake: Thinking semantic HTML replaces ARIA entirely.

question: When should you use <section> vs <article> vs <div>?
shortAnswer: <article> is self-contained content; <section> is a thematic grouping; <div> is a meaningless styling/scripting hook.
detailedAnswer: Use article for posts, cards, or widgets that make sense alone. Use section when a heading groups related content. Use div when you need a box with no semantic meaning. Overusing section without headings is an anti-pattern.

question: What is the difference between <header>, <head>, and heading elements?
shortAnswer: <head> is metadata; <header> is introductory page/section chrome; h1–h6 define outline hierarchy.
detailedAnswer: head lives in the document head and holds title, meta, links. header can appear in body for branding/nav or section intros. Heading levels should form a logical outline — don't skip levels for styling.

question: Why is a single <main> landmark important?
shortAnswer: It marks the primary content once per page so AT users can skip chrome.
detailedAnswer: Screen readers expose landmarks. Multiple mains confuse navigation. Hide repeated chrome outside main. Pair with skip links for keyboard users.

question: How do you structure a blog post with semantic HTML?
shortAnswer: article containing header (title/meta), optional nav for TOC, sections with headings, footer for author/related.
detailedAnswer: Keep one h1 for the page title. Nest sections under article. Use time with datetime for publish dates. Avoid wrapping the entire site in article.

question: What is the HTML outline and how do browsers treat heading levels?
shortAnswer: Authors should use heading levels for hierarchy; the historic outline algorithm is not reliably used by browsers/AT.
detailedAnswer: In practice, use visual and accessibility-friendly heading order. Don't rely on sectioning roots to reset heading ranks. Tools and AT mostly follow explicit h1–h6.

question: When is <aside> appropriate?
shortAnswer: For tangentially related content — sidebars, pull quotes, related links — not primary flow.
detailedAnswer: If removing aside breaks the main story, it probably shouldn't be aside. Site-global sidebars may be better as complementary landmarks with care.

question: Explain <nav> usage — one or many?
shortAnswer: Use nav for major navigation blocks; multiple navs are fine if labeled.
detailedAnswer: Primary site nav, TOC, and pagination can each be nav. Distinguish with aria-label. Don't wrap every link list in nav.

question: What are phrasing vs flow content, and why does it matter?
shortAnswer: Content categories constrain valid nesting — e.g. p cannot contain block-level flow like div.
detailedAnswer: Invalid nesting causes browsers to fix the DOM unexpectedly. Knowing categories prevents mysterious layout bugs and hydration mismatches.

question: How would you mark up a FAQ for accessibility and SEO?
shortAnswer: Use headings + content, or details/summary; consider FAQ schema in JSON-LD carefully.
detailedAnswer: Ensure keyboard access and visible focus. Don't fake accordions with non-button controls. Prefer progressive enhancement.

question: What is the role of <figure> and <figcaption>?
shortAnswer: Associate media with a caption as a single unit.
detailedAnswer: Useful for images, diagrams, code samples. Caption can be before/after media. Improves semantics vs orphaned text under an image.

question: When should you use <address>?
shortAnswer: For contact information for the nearest article or body author — not every postal address on the page.
detailedAnswer: Misusing address for arbitrary locations is common. It's specifically contact info for the document/section author.

question: Design a semantic layout for a dashboard with app chrome and widgets.
shortAnswer: banner/header + nav + main containing complementary widgets as sections/articles; avoid landmark spam.
detailedAnswer: Name regions. Keep one main. Self-contained widgets can be articles. Prefer headings inside widgets for AT navigation.
